description: Sync tasks, subtasks, comments and project overviews from the Asana projects you choose. Asana permissions are not imported.
opening: Sync tasks, subtasks, comments and project overviews from the Asana projects you select. Each task and subtask is one document. Each comment on a task is its own document, linked to the task. Each project is one overview page. Tasks link to their parent task, their projects and the tasks they block or are blocked by.

Asana permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. A task in two selected projects is stored once per project. Attachments, task activity other than comments, tags and custom fields are not synced. Items deleted in Asana can stay in HydraDB.

notes: Asana project privacy, project membership and per-task visibility are not reproduced. Set an access rule on each project that should be restricted.
A task in two selected projects is stored as one copy per project, and each copy follows its own project's rule.

connect.auth: Asana uses a personal access token. It has no scopes to choose: it sees what its user sees.
connect.credentials_note: Asana limits requests per token: 150 a minute on free domains and 1,500 on paid ones. A dedicated token keeps this connector from sharing that limit with other automations. To rotate it, create a new token, update the connector, check that a sync succeeds, then revoke the old token. Removing the token's user invalidates the token.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: In Asana's Developer Console, under My apps, Personal access tokens, create a token. A dedicated integration user works best. Add that user to every project you plan to select.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists every non-archived project in every workspace the token can see. Select the projects to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads what one token's Asana user can see, across that user's workspaces.

sync.first_sync: A newly selected project reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default, measured on when tasks and projects were last modified.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the tasks, subtasks and projects modified since the last sync. Comments are read again on every sync, without a time window.
sync.edits: An edited task or project is picked up through its modified time and updates its document. An edited comment is picked up because comments are read again on every sync.
sync.deletes: Tasks, comments and projects deleted in Asana can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: A project that refuses access on the first request is skipped and reported, and its unread window is kept for a later sync.

documents.name: Tasks and subtasks
documents.one_document: One task or subtask, as it appears in one selected project. Its comments are separate documents.
documents.title: The task name, or `Asana task` and its id when the name is empty.
documents.text: The task notes as plain text. A task with no notes gets a short summary instead: name, assignee, due date, status (`Open` or `Completed`) and projects. A subtask ends with a `Parent task` line that names its parent. The assignee, creation date, task key and parent are written as lines too. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the task was last modified, or when it was created if there is no modification time.
documents.files: Task attachments and their contents are not synced.

attributes.name: Task key
attributes.text: The selected project's id and the task's id. It keeps each project's copy of the task on its own document.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned user's display name, written as the `Assignee` line. The graph records that person as the assignee.

attributes.name: completed
attributes.text: Whether the task is done. Searchable as `Open` or `Completed` only in the summary of a task with no notes. It is not a filter.

attributes.name: due_at
attributes.text: The due time, or the due date. Searchable only in the summary of a task with no notes. It is not a filter.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the task was created, written into the task details. Sets the result date only when there is no modification time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the task was last modified. Sets the result date and decides when a sync picks the task up. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a subtask, its parent task, written as the `Parent` line. Links the subtask to its parent.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Display names of people @mentioned in the task notes. The graph records each as mentioned by the task. The field itself is not searchable, but the notes are.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.asana_gid
attributes.text: The task's Asana id. Picks out one task, in every project it was synced from. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.assignee_gid
attributes.text: The assigned user's Asana id. Limits a query to tasks assigned to one person. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `asana`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: completed_at
attributes.text: When the task was completed.

documents.name: Comments
documents.one_document: One comment on a task. A task in two selected projects has a copy of each comment per project.
documents.title: `Comment by <author> on <task name>`, leaving out whichever part is missing.
documents.text: The comment as plain text, then a `Parent task` line that names the task. The author, the posting time and the task's key are written with it.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The commenter's display name. The graph records the comment as written by that person.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the comment was posted, written as the `Created` line.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The key of the task the comment is on. Links the comment to that task.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Display names of people @mentioned in the comment. The graph records each as mentioned. The field itself is not searchable, but the comment text is.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.asana_gid
attributes.text: The comment's Asana id. Picks out one comment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.asana_task_gid
attributes.text: The Asana id of the task. Returns every comment on one task. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.author_gid
attributes.text: The commenter's Asana id. Limits a query to one person's comments. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `asana`. Not searchable.

documents.name: Projects
documents.one_document: One selected Asana project, as an overview page.
documents.title: The project name, or `Asana project` and its id when the name is empty.
documents.text: The project notes as plain text, then the title of the latest status update when Asana supplies one. A project with neither is written as `Project: <name>`. The modification time is written as the `Updated` line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the project was last modified, or when it was created if there is no modification time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the project was last modified, written as the `Updated` line. Sets the result date.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the project was created. Sets the result date only when there is no modification time. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.asana_gid
attributes.text: The project's Asana id. Picks out one project. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.asana_kind
attributes.text: Always `project`. Keeps or leaves out project overview pages. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.owner_gid
attributes.text: The project owner's Asana id. Limits a query to projects owned by one person. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `asana`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The project owner's display name. The owner is not added to the graph as a person.

attributes.name: completed
attributes.text: Whether the project is completed.

attributes.name: completed_at
attributes.text: When the project was completed.

attributes.name: due_at
attributes.text: The project due date.

attributes.name: type
attributes.text: Always `project`. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.asana_kind`.

example_searches: What tasks are assigned to Priya in the Q3 Launch project?
Which tasks are blocking the API migration task?
What does the Q3 Launch project brief say?

connections: A subtask to its parent task.
A task to each project it belongs to.
A task to each task it depends on, and to each task that depends on it.
No links to items in other tools.
people: People @mentioned in task notes and comments.
A project's owner is kept on the project but not added to the graph.
graph.from_text: Task notes, comment text and project notes.

not_synced: Projects you did not select. Archived projects are not listed for selection.
Task activity other than comments, such as assignments and field changes.
Sections, tags, custom fields and portfolios, including tag and custom-field values on tasks.
Comment likes, task followers and start dates.
Project status contents, apart from the latest status update's title.
Comments on a nested subtask that does not appear in its project's task list.
